TT- Booster.When to give: If received 2 TT doses in a pregnancy within the last 3 yrs*

BCG.When to give: At birth or as early as possible till one year of age

Hepatitis B - Birth dose.When to give: At birth or as early as possible within 24 hours

OPV-0.When to give: At birth or as early as possible within the first 15 days

OPV 1, 2 & 3.When to give: At 6 weeks, 10 weeks & 14 weeks (OPV can be given till 5 years of age)

Pentavalent 1, 2 & 3.When to give: At 6 weeks, 10 weeks & 14 weeks (can be given till one year of age)

Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV).When to give: Two primary doses at 6 weeks and 14 weeks. Booster dose at 9-12 months of age.

Rotavirus.When to give: At 6 weeks, 10 weeks & 14 weeks (can be given till one year of age)

IPV.When to give: Two fractional dose at 6 and 14 weeks of age

Measles/Measles-Rubella 1st dose#.When to give: 9 completed months-12 months. (Measles/Measles - Rubella can be given till 5 years of age)

Vitamin A (1st dose).When to give: At 9 completed months with measles- Rubella

Vitamin A*** (2nd to 9th dose).When to give: 16-18 months. Then one dose every 6 months up to the age of 5 years.

Notes.*: Give TT-2 or Booster doses before 36 weeks of pregnancy. However, give these even if more than 36 weeks have passed. Give TT to a woman in labour, if she has not previously received TT.
Notes.**: JE Vaccine is introduced in 230 endemic districts after the campaign.
Notes.***: The 2nd to 9th doses of Vitamin A can be administered to children 1-5 years old during biannual rounds, in collaboration with ICDS.
Notes.#: Phased introduction, presently in select states/districts
